title: Claude Max Pricing: Max 5x vs Max 20x Plans (2026)
summary: Claude Max pricing starts at $100 for 5x Pro usage, up to $200 for 20x limits. Compare plans to choose which fits your usage level and budget.
body_markdown:
## Moving repeated Claude tasks into Activepieces workflows


Put scheduled and triggered jobs in a workflow, not on a Max seat.


A workflow calls Claude by API and bills per token, which suits a job that runs when nobody is sitting down to work.


Activepieces is one place to build that: its published pricing is 1 credit per flow run however many steps the flow has, where Zapier bills per task and Make bills per module, as each lists on its own pricing page.


### Why scheduled automations don't suit a Claude subscription


Because a subscription is **priced for a person at a keyboard** , its ceiling is a rolling limit on that person's usage.


A job that sorts email at 6 a.m. or drafts a weekly report on Friday uses that allowance without anyone present, so it competes with your interactive work for the same limit.


You can end up locked out of Pro, and tempted by Max, because a background task ate the allowance.


Pay-per-token billing reverses that. You pay for what each run consumes, and the cost of a run is its input plus its output, which you can estimate before you commit.


> You can end up locked out of Pro, and tempted by Max, because a background task ate the allowance.


A short email-triage run costs a small, predictable amount, and a job that never runs costs nothing. No sales call is needed to work out the total.


The catch is that cost now scales with volume, so a flow that fires on every incoming message deserves a rough multiplication before you switch it on.


### Building a Claude step into a workflow


The flow in the screenshot shows the shape. Step 4 strips HTML from fetched page text, step 5, "Page Audit," is the AI step, and step 6 writes the result into a Google[Docs](https://docs.claude.com/en/docs/about-claude/models/overview) file.


Open the panel and you see that step's settings: a provider, a model, and a prompt that asks for an SEO audit, a score from 0 to 100, and a 120-word summary.


That example uses OpenAI's GPT-4o, but the step is the same kind of action, so pointing it at a Claude model is a change to the provider and model fields, using an Anthropic API key.


Two choices there control your bill. Pick the smallest model that does the job: Claude Haiku 5.5 suits high-volume sorting, while Claude Sonnet 5.5 suits summaries that need more judgment.


And strip the input first, as step 4 does, because tokens you never send are tokens you never pay for.


### What this doesn't replace


It doesn't replace Claude as a place to think.


Open-ended drafting, back-and-forth revision and exploratory coding still suit a subscription, and the lockout count still decides whether that subscription should be Pro or Max.


It also needs an API account, billed separately from any plan, and a workflow that fails quietly will keep spending until you notice, so check the first few runs by hand.
